content.text: Stripe's availability map covers 46 countries. PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. Gumroad holds payouts for up to 30 days in certain regions. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are unavailable across most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not temporary oversights waiting to be corrected — they are deliberate structural decisions built into conventional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/why-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/usdt-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-methods-filipino-digital-creators-stack-started-generating|COREMERCH guide to payment]]-gateways-digital-products-what-actually-how-2|USDT Payment]]-solutions-zimbabwean-digital-sellers-costing-you|payment]] infrastructure designed for Western banking systems. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is building on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Digital paypal

Each of these platforms offers a unique set of tools and features designed to facilitate digital sales. However, when it comes to restricted countries, these options become severely limited. Stripe, for instance, operates in 46 countries out of 195 on earth, leaving a significant portion of the global market without access. Meanwhile, PayPal account suspensions can hold funds for up to 180 days with no appeal, rendering it an unreliable option for many creators.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

In countries where Stripe and PayPal are restricted, creators are forced to look for alternative payment gateways. Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy, while popular options, also have their own set of limitations. They may not be available in certain countries or may have restrictions on the types of digital products that can be sold. This leaves creators with limited choices, often resulting in a diminished user experience and lower sales.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

When it comes to payment speed, fees, and real costs, the options become even more complicated. Stripe and PayPal, while offering faster payment processing, come with higher fees and stricter regulations. Alternative options like NOWPayments, on the other hand, offer lower fees and greater flexibility, but may not be as widely accepted. This raises questions about the true cost of each option and whether it aligns with the creator's needs and goals.
Traditional platforms often come with hidden fees and strict regulations.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

The asymmetric risk of platform dependency becomes concrete only when the platform acts. While a PayPal or Stripe account is functioning normally, the risk feels theoretical and distant. When it stops functioning — through suspension, policy change, or geographic restriction enforcement — the creator loses their revenue channel instantly, often with funds already inside the platform that cannot be withdrawn. The conventional appeals process rarely reverses these decisions because the original decision was made algorithmically and the human review process operates on the platform's timeline and criteria, not yours. Sovereign infrastructure eliminates this asymmetry entirely. Your Cloudflare Pages storefront cannot be suspended by a payment processor's compliance decision. Your wallet cannot be frozen by anyone.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

The storefront in a COREMERCH deployment is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. It costs nothing to host. It scales to any traffic level automatically. It cannot be taken down by a payment platform's compliance decision because the hosting and the payment layer are completely separate infrastructure. Your buyer experience is clean and professional — a product page, a crypto checkout with QR code generation and live price feeds, and an automatic delivery email within 30 seconds of payment. Every component runs under your own accounts. If COREMERCH closed tomorrow, every store deployed would continue running exactly as it does today. That is what infrastructure ownership means.
How do I sell digital products if Stripe is not available in my country?

What's the most important thing to consider when choosing an e-commerce infrastructure? The answer is ownership. Creators should prioritize infrastructure that puts them in control, allowing them to maintain ownership and control over their digital assets. This ensures that they can manage their products, store them securely, and deliver them efficiently, without relying on external platforms or gateways.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure offers greater flexibility and ownership for creators.
